mainTopic: Returning found court documents and loan notes, and רב's ruling that a סמפון found with the lender is invalid.
overview: The amud opens with the end of רב הונא's worry that there may be two towns called שוירי, so a found גט should not be returned. רבה finds a משנה saying that any court document is returned. When רב עמרם objects that money cases cannot teach about איסור, רבה shows that the same משנה lists חליצה and מיאון documents. After a short story about the cracked beam in the study hall, the גמרא explains the words חפיסה and דלוסקמא. It then defines a roll and a bundle of documents, rejects a proof that a knot is a סימן, and works out what the finder announces. Next the גמרא explains why notes of one borrower from three lenders go back to the borrower, and why notes of three borrowers from one lender go back to the lender. Finally, רב rules that a סמפון found with the lender is invalid. The גמרא defends his ruling against several challenges, mostly by saying the סמפון was found among torn documents. Its answer to the last challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב הונא worries there may be two towns named שוירי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that we worry there might be two towns called שוירי, so the found גט cannot be safely returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are concerned that there may be two places called שוירי.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of רב הונא's ruling about a גט found in his בית דין. He says we must worry that another town has the same name, so the גט might belong to a different couple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גט names a town, שוירי, but a matching name does not prove a matching person if two towns share that name. Because of this doubt, רב הונא holds the גט should not be handed over. The next steps test this worry against a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned / we take the worry seriously
שוירי, the name of a town written in the גט

phrases.english: We are concerned for two places called Sheviri.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא's ruling on the found גט, which started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because there may be two towns named שוירי, a found גט naming שוירי is not returned.

steps.title: רב חסדא tells רבה to look into the matter
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells רבה to research the question because רב הונא will ask him about it that evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to רבה: Go out and look into this, because tonight רב הונא will ask you about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. רב חסדא sends רבה to find a source that decides the question of the found גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is decided yet in this step. It only shows that the ruling was being checked, and it prepares us for the source רבה will find.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out and examine / look into it

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to Rabba:
Go out and examine it,

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְאוּרְתָּא בָּעֵי לַהּ רַב הוּנָא מִינָּךְ.
phrases.english: for in the evening Rav Huna will ask it of you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַבָּה: פּוֹק עַיֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sends רבה to test רב הונא's ruling against the sources.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling; this is an instruction that sets up the search for a source.

steps.title: רבה finds a משנה: court documents are returned
steps.stepSummary: רבה finds a משנה saying that any document done by a בית דין must be returned, which suggests the found גט should be returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went out, looked carefully, and found it, as we learned in a משנה: any document of the בית דין, the finder must return it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a משנה to settle the question. It says that court documents are returned to their owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט found in the בית דין counts as a court document. The משנה says such documents are returned, so the worry about two towns named שוירי does not stop the return. This works against רב הונא's worry.

keyTerms.meaning: A document or act carried out by the court

phrases.english: He went out, examined carefully, and found,
as we learned: any court document,
he must return it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out רב חסדא's instruction by bringing a source.
steps.raayaObject: That the גט found in בית דין should be returned, despite the worry of two שוירי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: כל מעשה בית דין הרי זה יחזיר.

steps.title: רב עמרם: you can't learn an איסור case from a ממון case
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם challenges רבה: a גט is a question of איסור, but the משנה seems to deal with ממון, so how can one be learned from the other?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said to רבה: How can the Master decide a question of איסור from a source about ממון?
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם attacks רבה's proof. He says the משנה is about money documents, while a גט touches on forbidden relationships.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In money matters a mistake only costs money, but with a גט a mistake could permit a married woman to remarry. So we may be stricter with a גט than with money documents. If so, the משנה about money cannot prove anything about a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: Matters of איסור (what is forbidden or permitted)

phrases.english: Rav Amram said to Rabba:
How does the Master resolve
a prohibition matter from a money matter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof brought in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's proof from the משנה about court documents.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט is a matter of איסור, where we may be stricter, so a rule about money documents cannot be applied to it.

steps.title: רבה: the same משנה lists חליצה and מיאון documents
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers sharply that the משנה itself includes שטרי חליצה and מיאונין, which are matters of איסור, so the rule covers איסור too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Fool! We learned in that משנה 'documents of חליצה and מיאונין.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends his proof. He points out that the משנה is not only about money, because it also lists חליצה and מיאון documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליצה and מיאון decide whether a woman may marry, so they are matters of איסור, just like a גט. Since the משנה says to return those documents too, it already applies to איסור. רב עמרם's challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Fool (literally, a beet): a sharp insult
Documents of refusal, when a young girl married off by her mother or brothers rejects the marriage

phrases.english: He said to him: Fool,
we learned 'documents of chalitzah and refusals.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תְּרָדָא, שְׁטָרֵי חֲלִיצָה וּמֵיאוּנִין תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב עמרם's challenge from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the source already covers the type of case the challenger thought it left out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is only about money documents, so it cannot teach about a גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה includes documents of חליצה and מיאון, which are איסור matters, so the rule of returning court documents applies to a גט as well.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה proves that a document found in בית דין is returned, even in an איסור case, because the משנה itself lists חליצה and מיאון documents.

steps.title: The study hall beam cracks, and each sage blames the insult
steps.stepSummary: The cedar beam of the study hall cracked. Each sage said it cracked because of his own hurt honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: The cedar beam of the study hall split. One Sage said: It split because of my fortune. And the other Sage said: It split because of my fortune.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story told after the sharp exchange. When the beam cracked, each of the two sages believed it was a sign on his behalf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה had called רב עמרם a fool, while רב עמרם had challenged רבה's ruling. Each one felt the other had wronged him, and each saw the cracked beam as a sign from heaven in his favor. The story shows how seriously the honor of a תלמיד חכם is taken.

phrases.english: The cedar beam of the study hall split.

phrases.aramaic: מָר אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם לַתַּאי דִּידִי פְּקַע.
phrases.english: One Sage said: Because of my fortune it split.
phrases.notes: Each one means that heaven was standing up for him because the other had wronged him.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם לַתַּאי דִּידִי פְּקַע.
phrases.english: And the other Sage said: Because of my fortune it split.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that follows the sharp exchange between רבה and רב עמרם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling; the story shows each sage believed heaven took his side over the hurt to his honor.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: what is a חפיסה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about documents found in a חפיסה or a דלוסקמא, and asks what a חפיסה is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If he found documents in a חפיסה or in a דלוסקמא. What is a חפיסה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and starts a new topic. It asks for the meaning of an unusual word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that documents found inside a container are returned. To understand the case we need to know what these containers are, so the גמרא asks about each word.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of container mentioned in the משנה
Another type of container mentioned in the משנה

phrases.english: If he found documents in a chafisa or in a deluskema.
What is a chafisa?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָצָא בַּחֲפִיסָה אוֹ בִדְלוֹסְקָמָא. מַאי חֲפִיסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to explain the next words of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word חפיסה.

steps.title: A חפיסה is a small leather flask
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה explains that a חפיסה is a small leather flask.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: It is a small leather flask.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. A חפיסה is a small flask made of leather.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we can picture the case in the משנה: documents found rolled up inside a small flask. The container ties the documents together as one find.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: חֵמֶת קְטַנָּה.
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana says: A small leather flask.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: חֵמֶת קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A חפיסה is a small leather flask.

steps.title: What is a דלוסקמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the second word in the משנה, דלוסקמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a דלוסקמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the second container mentioned in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the question about חפיסה. Each unusual word in the משנה gets its own explanation.

phrases.english: What is a deluskema?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first word of the משנה to the second.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word דלוסקמא.

steps.title: A דלוסקמא is a bag used by old people
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל explains that a דלוסקמא is a bag or container used by old people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שמואל said: It is a bag of the elderly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: a דלוסקמא is a container that old people carry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With both words explained, the case in the משנה is clear: documents found inside a small flask or an old person's bag are returned.
steps.whatToRemember: חפיסה is a small leather flask, and דלוסקמא is an old person's bag. Both are containers in which documents might be found.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל: טְלִיקָא דְסָבֵי.
phrases.english: Rabba bar Shmuel says: A bag of the elderly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל: טְלִיקָא דְסָבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A דלוסקמא is a bag used by the elderly.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines a roll and a bundle of documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה, 'a roll of documents or a bundle of documents.' A ברייתא explains that each one means three documents: a roll is three rolled together, and a bundle is three tied together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A roll of documents or a bundle of documents, etc.' The Rabbis taught in a ברייתא: How many documents make a roll? Three rolled together. How many make a bundle? Three tied together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה. Then it brings a ברייתא that defines the two terms 'roll' and 'bundle.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both terms need at least three documents. The difference given here is how they are held together. A roll is held by being rolled, and a bundle is held by being tied. The word 'tied' is what the גמרא will try to build on in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A roll: documents rolled up together

phrases.english: A roll of documents
or a bundle of documents, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
How many make up a roll of documents?
Three, rolled up with one another.
And how many make up a bundle of documents?
Three, tied to one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כַּמָּה הוּא תַּכְרִיךְ שֶׁל שְׁטָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from defining חפיסה and דלוסקמא to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A roll is three documents rolled together. A bundle is three documents tied together.

steps.title: Inference: a knot counts as an identifying sign
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא's word 'tied,' the גמרא concludes that a קשר (knot) counts as a סימן. The owner could describe the knot to prove the bundle is his.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that a knot is a סימן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to pull a new rule out of the ברייתא: a knot can serve as a סימן for returning a lost object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bundle must be returned, and the ברייתא says what makes it a bundle is that it is tied. So it seems the knot is what lets the owner identify it. That would mean a knot is a valid סימן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Learn from this': a conclusion drawn from a source
An identifying sign the owner uses to claim a lost item

steps.whyThisMatters: If a knot is a סימן, then any found item that is tied in a special way would have to be announced and returned to whoever describes the knot.

phrases.english: Learn from this
that a knot is an identifying sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a legal rule from the word 'tied' in the ברייתא of step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That a knot (קשר) counts as a סימן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא defining a bundle as three documents tied together

steps.title: Rejection: רבי חייא's version says 'rolled,' not 'tied'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. רבי חייא teaches the ברייתא differently: the bundle is three documents rolled together. So the ברייתא never mentions a knot, and nothing can be proven about knots.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי חייא teaches: three rolled together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 12. It shows that another version of the ברייתא says 'rolled' instead of 'tied.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole proof depended on the word 'tied.' In רבי חייא's version, the bundle is identified by how it is rolled, not by a knot. Without the word 'tied,' there is no proof that a knot is a סימן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But it was taught': brings a source to push back

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חייא is not arguing about the law of knots. He simply has a different wording of the ברייתא, and that removes the proof.

phrases.english: But רבי חייא teaches:
Three, rolled up with one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that a knot is a סימן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof relied on the word 'tied,' but רבי חייא's version says 'rolled.'

steps.title: Then a bundle is the same as a roll
steps.stepSummary: If a bundle is also 'three rolled together,' it sounds exactly like a roll. Why would the משנה list both?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is the same as a roll!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חייא's wording. If a bundle is also rolled, it seems identical to a roll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists 'roll' and 'bundle' as two separate cases. In רבי חייא's version, both are three documents rolled together. So it looks like the משנה repeated itself for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so': opens a challenge based on what was just said

phrases.english: If so,
isn't that the same as a roll?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording brought in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's version, which describes a bundle as 'rolled together'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both roll and bundle are rolled, there is no difference between them, and the משנה should not list them separately.

steps.title: The difference: chained in a row versus stacked and rolled
steps.stepSummary: A roll means each document starts at the head of the one before it, so they are rolled in a chain. A bundle means the documents are stacked one on top of another and then rolled. Both are rolled, but they are arranged differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a roll, each one is placed at the top of the next one. In a bundle, they are placed on top of each other and rolled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows that roll and bundle are two different arrangements, even though both are rolled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a roll, the documents are laid out end to end, each one starting where the last one ends, and then rolled. In a bundle, they are stacked in a pile and rolled up together. So the משנה is not repeating itself, and רבי חייא's wording still stands without needing a knot.

keyTerms.meaning: At the head of the other one
Placed on top of one another

steps.whatToRemember: Both roll and bundle need three documents. In רבי חייא's version both are rolled. A roll is laid end to end, and a bundle is stacked. The attempt to prove that a knot is a סימן was rejected.

phrases.english: A roll is where each and every one
is at the head of the other one,
a bundle is where they are placed on top of one another
(and rolled).
phrases.notes: Some versions have this word and some don't. Either way, the bundle is a stack rather than a chain.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּכְרִיךְ כֹּל חַד וְחַד בְּרֵאשֵׁהּ דְּחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: two different arrangements of rolled documents
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A roll and a bundle, both rolled, seemed to be identical.
steps.terutzMaskana: A roll is documents laid end to end and rolled. A bundle is documents stacked on each other and rolled.

steps.title: What does the finder announce?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the finder of the roll or bundle of documents calls out, so the real owner can come and claim it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does he announce?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple practical question about the finder's announcement. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who finds a lost object must announce it, and the owner must then identify it. The גמרא wants to know what exactly the finder says about a roll or bundle of documents, because that decides what the owner still has to describe.

keyTerms.meaning: announces, calls out publicly (that he found something)

phrases.english: What does he announce?
phrases.notes: 'He' is the person who found the roll or bundle of documents from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining a roll and a bundle in steps 11-15, the גמרא now asks how such a find is announced.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the finder of a roll or bundle of documents says in his announcement.

steps.title: First answer: he announces the number
steps.stepSummary: The first answer is that the finder announces how many documents he found. The owner then identifies them by how they were rolled.
steps.simpleTranslation: He announces the number.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the finder calls out the number of documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the finder already reveals the number, the owner cannot use the number as his sign. The owner would have to identify the documents by something else, such as the way they were rolled together.

keyTerms.meaning: an identifying sign the owner gives to prove the object is his

phrases.english: The number.
phrases.notes: The finder says, 'I found three documents,' and the owner then proves they are his by describing how they were rolled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The finder announces the number of documents; the owner identifies them by how they were rolled.

steps.title: Then why does the משנה say three?
steps.stepSummary: If the finder announces the number and the owner identifies the documents by how they were rolled, two documents would work just as well. So why does the משנה say three?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why specifically three? Even two would also work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 17. That answer makes the משנה's number 'three' seem unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under step 17, the number is not the owner's sign at all, because the finder already said it. The owner's sign is the rolling, and two documents can be rolled together too. So the משנה should have said 'two,' and the word 'three' seems to have no purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: why specifically this? (why mention this detail?)

phrases.english: Why specifically three?
Even two as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִרְיָא תְּלָתָא אֲפִילּוּ תְּרֵין נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the finder announces the number of documents.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the number is announced, it cannot be the owner's sign. The משנה's 'three' would then serve no purpose, since two rolled documents could be returned the same way.

steps.title: Like רבינא: he announces only 'documents'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the first answer. Like רבינא's rule for coins, the finder announces only 'documents,' and the owner must give the exact number as his sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, as רבינא said: one announces 'coins.' Here too, he announces 'documents.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. The finder says only that he found 'documents,' without giving a number, just as רבינא said a finder of coins says only 'coins.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the number becomes the owner's sign, together with the rolling. The plural word 'documents' already tells everyone there are at least two. So if the owner says 'two,' he adds nothing, and that is why the משנה needs three.
steps.whatToRemember: The finder announces only the general type of item ('documents'). The owner must supply the details, including the exact number, and 'three' counts as a real sign because the plural already implies two.

phrases.english: Rather, as Ravina said:
He announces 'coins.'
Here too, he announces 'documents.'
phrases.notes: Since 'documents' is plural, two is already understood. Only 'three' gives the owner a real sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 17 and solves the problem raised in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the earlier answer with a different reading of what is announced.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The finder announces the number, so 'three' seems pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The finder announces only 'documents.' The owner must give the number, and three is the smallest number that adds real information beyond the plural.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: one borrower from three lenders
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that if one person borrowed from three lenders, the found notes go back to the borrower.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: one who borrowed from three people, return them to the borrower, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה and quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is three loan notes found together, each with the same borrower but a different lender. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that they are given to the borrower, not to any of the lenders.

keyTerms.meaning: borrower, the one who took the loan
etc.; the quote from the משנה continues

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One who borrowed from three
should return them to the borrower, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר אֶחָד הַלֹּוֶה מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה יַחְזִיר לַלֹּוֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of announcing documents and quotes the next ruling in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three notes of one borrower owed to three different lenders, found together, are returned to the borrower.

steps.title: Why the notes go to the borrower
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the reason: if the notes belonged to the three lenders, there would be no reason for them to be together in one place.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think they belong to the lenders, what are they doing together?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling. The fact that the notes were found together shows whose they are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three separate lenders would each keep their own note, so their notes would not end up in the same place. The only person who has a link to all three notes is the borrower. So finding them together points to him as the one who lost them.

keyTerms.meaning: if it enters your mind, if you were to think

steps.whatToRemember: Where the documents were found can be evidence. Three lenders' notes would not be together, so the notes are presumed to have been lost by the one borrower.

phrases.english: For if it enters your mind
that they belong to the lenders,
what are they doing together?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּמַלְוִין נִינְהוּ מַאי בָּעוּ גַּבֵּי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the ruling quoted in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That the notes belong to (were lost by) the borrower.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logical point that three different lenders' notes would not be found together.

steps.title: Maybe the three lenders took their notes to court together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reasoning from step 21. The three lenders might have gone to court together to get their notes ratified, and the notes could have been lost there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps the three lenders went together to have their notes ratified in court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the reason that the three lenders' notes would never be in one place. It suggests a real situation where they could be together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said three separate lenders have no reason to keep their notes together, so the borrower must have lost them. The גמרא answers that a trip to court for קיום שטרות could bring all three notes to one place. If so, a lender may have lost them, and the proof that they belong to the borrower falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe. It opens a possible objection.
Ratification. The court confirms the witnesses' signatures on a document.

phrases.english: Perhaps they went to have them ratified?
phrases.notes: "They" means the three lenders, taking their notes to court together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning given in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that three lenders' notes would never be together in one place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A shared trip to court for ratification gives a real reason for the notes to be together. That means a lender could be the one who lost them.

steps.title: The notes are already ratified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה speaks about notes that already carry the court's ratification.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where the notes are already ratified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying these notes already have the court's ratification on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ratification is already written on the notes, the court visit is over. Each lender would have taken his own note home, so the court trip no longer explains why the notes are together.

keyTerms.meaning: They are ratified. The court's confirmation is already on them.

phrases.english: Where they are ratified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The notes might have been together on their way to the court for ratification.
steps.terutzMaskana: The notes are already ratified, so that trip is finished and does not explain why they are together.

steps.title: Maybe they fell from the court scribe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. After ratifying the notes, maybe the court's scribe still had all three and dropped them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps the notes fell from the hand of the court scribe after he ratified them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. Even ratified notes might still have been sitting together with the scribe who ratified them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 assumed that after ratification each lender takes his note home. This challenge says the scribe may have kept them for a while, so the notes could be together and the borrower would not be the one who lost them.

keyTerms.meaning: The scribe, here the court's scribe

phrases.english: Perhaps they fell from the hand of the scribe?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that ratified notes go straight back to each lender.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The scribe may still have held all three ratified notes together and lost them.

steps.title: People don't leave ratified notes with the scribe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that people do not leave their ratified notes with the scribe. So the borrower is the likely one who lost them.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person does not leave his ratified note in the hand of the scribe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge based on how people normally act. Once a note is ratified, its owner takes it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ratified note is valuable, so no lender lets it stay with the scribe. That removes the last way the three lenders' notes could end up together. The ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, that they go back to the borrower, stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaves, lets something stay for a while

steps.whatToRemember: Notes of one borrower from three lenders go back to the borrower. Three separate lenders have no normal reason to have their notes together: not a court visit, and not the scribe.

phrases.english: A person does not leave his ratified note
in the hand of the scribe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24 and closes this line.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The scribe might have been holding all three ratified notes.
steps.terutzMaskana: People take their ratified notes right away, so the scribe would not have had them.

steps.title: The next case: three borrowers from one lender
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה. If three people borrowed from one lender, the found notes go back to the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: If three people borrowed from one lender, the finder should return the notes to the lender, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on and quotes the next case in the משנה. It is setting up an explanation of why this case goes to the lender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the previous case. Now the one person in common is the lender, and the משנה says the notes go back to him.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on. The rest of the quote is left out.

phrases.english: Three who borrowed from one
he should return to the lender, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה after closing the previous case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Notes of three borrowers from one lender are returned to the lender.

steps.title: Why the notes would not be with the borrowers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the reason: if the notes belonged to the three borrowers, they would have no reason to be together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if you think these notes belong to the borrowers, what would they be doing together?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for the lender getting the notes. Three separate borrowers would not keep their notes in one place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A borrower would hold his note only after paying it back. Three different borrowers would each keep their own note separately. The one person who would naturally hold all three is the lender, so he must be the one who lost them.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind, you might think

phrases.english: For if it enters your mind that they belong to the borrowers,
what are they doing together?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ruling quoted in step 26, the same way step 21 explained step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that the notes go back to the lender.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: three separate borrowers would not have their notes together, but the one lender would.

steps.title: Maybe the borrowers went to one scribe together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reason. Maybe the three borrowers went to the same scribe to have their notes written, and the notes were lost together.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps they went together to have the notes written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way the notes could have been together before they ever reached the lender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one scribe wrote all three notes at once, they could have been lost together before being handed to the lender. Then being together would not prove that the lender lost them.

phrases.english: Perhaps they went to have them written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only the lender would have all three notes together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The notes could have been together at one scribe's place while being written, before the lender ever got them.

steps.title: Three different scribes wrote them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the notes are in the handwriting of three different scribes, so they were not written together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where the notes are written in the handwriting of three different scribes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge by narrowing the case. Each note was written by a different scribe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three different handwritings show the notes were not made together at one scribe. So the only person who would naturally hold all three is the lender, and the notes go back to him.
steps.whatToRemember: Notes of three borrowers from one lender go back to the lender, because only he would hold all three. The case is where three different scribes wrote them.

phrases.english: Where they are written in the hands of three scribes.
phrases.notes: "Hands" here means handwriting. Each note was clearly written by a different scribe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The notes may have been together at one scribe while being written.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three different scribes wrote them, so they were never together at one scribe.

steps.title: Maybe the borrowers went to have the notes ratified together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another way the three borrowers' notes could have ended up together: they all took them to court for ratification.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps the three borrowers went to the court to have their notes ratified, and lost them there together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises one more challenge to the reason that the notes belong to the lender. Even with three different scribes, the borrowers might have met at court to get their notes ratified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 showed that the notes were not written together. Now the גמרא suggests they could have been gathered together later, at the court, during ratification. If so, the borrowers could be the ones who lost them, and the notes being together would not prove they came from the lender.

keyTerms.meaning: And perhaps; opens a possible alternative explanation
To ratify them; to have the court confirm the witnesses' signatures
Ratification of documents by a בית דין

phrases.english: But perhaps they went to have them ratified?
phrases.notes: "They" means the three borrowers, who might have taken their notes to court together and lost them there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new way around the answer of step 29
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason in step 27 that the borrowers' notes would have no reason to be together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Different scribes do not rule out the notes being gathered later, when all three borrowers brought them to court for ratification.

steps.title: Only the lender ratifies a loan note
steps.stepSummary: The lender is the one who has a note ratified, not the borrower, so the borrowers would not have brought the notes to court.
steps.simpleTranslation: A lender ratifies his note. A borrower does not ratify his note.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that getting a note ratified is something only the lender does. So the borrowers would never have taken the notes to court together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ratifying a note helps the person who will collect with it, and that is the lender. A borrower has no interest in strengthening a document against himself. So the ratification idea only fits the lender, and the ruling that the notes go back to the lender stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Ratifies; has the document confirmed in court

steps.whatToRemember: Three notes from three borrowers to one lender go back to the lender. They were not written together (three scribes), and borrowers do not bring notes to court for ratification.

phrases.english: A lender ratifies his note,
a borrower does not ratify his note.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַלְוֶה מְקַיֵּים שְׁטָרֵיהּ, לֹוֶה לָא מְקַיֵּים שְׁטָרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: only one side has a reason to ratify
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The borrowers might have gathered the notes together at court for ratification.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a lender ratifies a note, so the notes being together points to the lender.

steps.title: The משנה's rule about סמפונות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if there are סמפונות with the documents, one follows what they say.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there are cancellation notes among the documents, one should do what is written in the cancellation notes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, about סמפונות, which are notes showing a debt was paid or canceled. This line sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if a סמפון is found among the documents, we act on it, meaning we treat the debt as paid. The open question is whose possession the סמפון is in, and the coming steps depend on that.

keyTerms.meaning: A document showing that a debt was paid or canceled, like a receipt
He should act on what the סמפונות say

phrases.english: If there are cancellation notes with them –
he should do what is in the cancellation notes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם יֵשׁ עִמָּהֶן סִמְפּוֹנוֹת יַעֲשֶׂה מָה שֶׁבַּסִּמְפּוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the found-notes case to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If סמפונות are found with the documents, we follow what they say.

steps.title: רב: a סמפון in the lender's hands is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a סמפון coming out of the lender's possession is invalid, even if it is in the lender's own handwriting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רב: A cancellation note that comes out of the lender's possession, even if it is written in his own handwriting, is like a joke and is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling of רב about a סמפון found with the lender. רב says we do not trust it, even if the lender wrote it himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a סמפון would be with the borrower, since he received it when he paid. If it is still with the lender, maybe it was never handed over because the debt was never paid. So רב treats it like something written without meaning, and it does not cancel the debt.

keyTerms.meaning: That comes out of the lender's possession
Like someone joking; not a serious act

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב suspects forgery. He accepts the lender wrote it. The problem is that it may have been written ahead of time and the debt never paid.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
A cancellation note that comes out from the possession of a lender,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּכְתַב יָדוֹ –
phrases.english: even though it is written in his own handwriting –
it is only like one who is joking, and it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an אמורא's ruling on the topic of the משנה line just quoted
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סמפון found in the lender's possession is invalid, even in his own handwriting.

steps.title: Why even the lender's own handwriting does not help
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that a scribe's handwriting is obviously suspect, and even the lender's own handwriting is too, because he may have written it early to be ready for payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious when a scribe wrote it, because we can say the lender happened to have a scribe around and had him write it. But even if the lender wrote it himself, it is invalid. He may have thought: perhaps the borrower will come at twilight on Friday and pay me. If I do not give him a receipt, he will not give me the money. So I will write one now, and when he brings the money I will give it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the חידוש in רב's ruling. It shows why even a סמפון the lender wrote himself proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a scribe's handwriting, it is easy to say the lender just used the chance while a scribe was available. With the lender's own handwriting, we might think he would only write it after being paid. The גמרא answers that he may have written it early, worried the borrower would come right before שבת, when writing is forbidden, and refuse to pay without a receipt.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed to say; this case is obvious, the next one is the real חידוש
Twilight; here, the time just before שבת begins

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, a סמפון still held by the lender proves nothing, even in his own handwriting, because he may have prepared it ahead of time.

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִבַּעְיָא כָּתוּב בִּכְתַב יַד סוֹפֵר,
phrases.english: It is not necessary to say this when it is written in a scribe's handwriting,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר סָפְרָא אִתְרְמִי לֵיהּ וּכְתַב,
phrases.english: since one can say a scribe happened to be available to him and he wrote it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ כָּתוּב בִּכְתַב יָדוֹ פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: but even when it is written in his own handwriting, it is invalid.
He thought: perhaps he will happen to come
at twilight and pay me,
phrases.notes: This is twilight right before שבת, when the lender could not write a receipt anymore.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי לָא יָהֵיבְנָא לֵיהּ לָא יָהֵיב לִי זוּזֵי,
phrases.english: and if I do not give him a receipt, he will not give me the money,
so I will write it now,
so that when he brings me my money, I will give it to him.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, "brings."

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא מִבַּעְיָא כָּתוּב בִּכְתַב יַד סוֹפֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning and the חידוש of רב's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a סמפון in the lender's own handwriting is invalid, because he may have written it in advance.

steps.title: Challenge to רב from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב from the משנה, which says to follow the סמפונות found with the documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If there are cancellation notes with them, he should do what is in the cancellation notes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to challenge רב using the משנה. The משנה seems to say a סמפון found with the lender's documents is trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case seems to be documents in the lender's possession, and it says to follow the סמפון. That looks like the opposite of רב, who said such a סמפון is invalid. The גמרא will need to answer this.

phrases.english: We learned: If there are cancellation notes with them,
phrases.notes: The point of the challenge is left unsaid: the משנה seems to be about notes found with the lender, which רב called invalid.

phrases.english: he should do what is in the cancellation notes.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: אִם יֵשׁ עִמָּהֶן סִמְפּוֹנוֹת, יַעֲשֶׂה מָה שֶׁבְּסִמְפּוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a סמפון from the lender's possession is invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה seems to describe סמפונות found among the lender's documents and says to act on them, which contradicts רב.

steps.title: The receipt was found among torn documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from our משנה. It uses רב ספרא's explanation that the סמפון was found among torn documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב ספרא said: it was found among torn documents. Here too, he found it among torn documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by saying our משנה is talking about a special case. In that case the receipt was lying among torn, cancelled documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a receipt in the lender's hands is suspect, because he may have written it early. But if he put it among torn notes, he himself treated the debt as paid. So the משנה trusts the receipt only in that case, and רב's general rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Torn documents, meaning notes that were already cancelled

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא uses this same answer for the next two challenges against רב (steps 38 and 40). The fourth challenge, from a ברייתא, gets a different answer (step 42).

phrases.english: As Rav Safra said:
that it was found among torn documents,
here too,
it is where he found it among torn documents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 35
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to trust any סמפון found with the lender's documents.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה trusts it only when it was found among torn documents, so רב's rule is untouched.

steps.title: Challenge from the case of two men named יוסף בן שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה in which a receipt found among a lender's documents cancels debts. This seems to contradict רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If a person found among his documents a receipt saying 'The note of יוסף בן שמעון is repaid,' the notes of both of them are considered repaid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה to challenge רב. That משנה treats a receipt found among the lender's own papers as valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender has two debtors with the same name, יוסף בן שמעון. The receipt doesn't say which one it means, so both are treated as paid. That only makes sense if a receipt found in the lender's possession counts, which is the opposite of רב's ruling.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If one found among his documents

phrases.aramaic: שְׁטָרוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן פָּרוּעַ –
phrases.english: "The note of Yosef ben Shimon is repaid"
phrases.notes: The case is a lender with two debtors who both have this name, which is why the next line says "both of them."

phrases.english: the notes of both of them are repaid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, a new source is brought against רב
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a סמפון from the lender's possession is invalid (step 33)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה uses a receipt found among the lender's documents to cancel debts, so such a receipt must be valid.

steps.title: Same answer: it was found among torn documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the second challenge the same way. This receipt, too, was found among torn documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב ספרא said: it was found among torn documents. Here too, it was found among torn documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reuses רב ספרא's answer. It explains the יוסף בן שמעון case as one where the receipt was among cancelled papers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the logic. The same limit is applied to a second משנה, so רב's rule survives again. Placing the receipt among torn notes shows the lender himself considered the debt paid.

phrases.english: As Rav Safra said:
that it was found among torn documents,
here too,
it is where it was found among torn documents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 37 using the answer from step 36
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יוסף בן שמעון משנה seemed to trust any receipt among the lender's papers.
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers only to a receipt found among torn documents.

steps.title: Challenge from the orphans' oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the wording of the oath that orphans take before collecting their father's debt. Part of the oath is that they found no receipt among their father's documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "An oath that our father did not instruct us, and that our father did not tell us, and that we did not find among our father's documents, that this note is repaid."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a third challenge against רב by quoting the orphans' oath. This step sets up the challenge; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The orphans must swear they did not find a receipt among their father's documents. That suggests finding one would stop them from collecting. If so, a receipt found in the lender's own possession counts, which seems to go against רב.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"An oath that father did not instruct us,
phrases.notes: Orphans swear this before collecting a debt owed to their late father. It is a משנה in שבועות.

phrases.english: and that father did not tell us,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁלֹּא מָצָאנוּ בֵּין שְׁטָרוֹתָיו שֶׁל אַבָּא
phrases.english: and that we did not find among father's documents
that this note is repaid."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third source is brought against רב after the second challenge was answered
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a סמפון from the lender's possession is invalid (step 33)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The oath implies that a receipt found among the father's (lender's) documents would block collection, so such a receipt must be valid.

steps.title: The orphans' oath also refers to torn documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from the orphans' oath with רב ספרא's explanation: the receipt was found among torn documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: it is talking about a receipt found among torn documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the orphans' oath. It uses the same answer as before: the receipt was found among torn documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath seemed to show that a receipt found among the father's papers would cancel the debt, which goes against רב. The answer is that the oath means a receipt found among torn documents. Torn documents are papers that were already paid off and cancelled, so a receipt among them is believable.

keyTerms.meaning: Torn documents, meaning papers that were already cancelled

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
That it was found among torn documents.
phrases.notes: This is the same answer the גמרא already used for the first two challenges (steps 36 and 38).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא: שֶׁנִּמְצָא בֵּין שְׁטָרוֹת קְרוּעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the orphans' oath in step 39.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the receipt was among torn documents.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The oath suggests any receipt among the father's papers would cancel the debt, which goes against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oath only means a receipt found among torn documents, so רב's view still stands.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a receipt with witnesses is confirmed by its signers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a סמפון with witnesses on it is confirmed through its signatures. This seems to treat it as valid even when it comes from the lender's papers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A receipt that has witnesses signed on it is confirmed by means of its signers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge against רב from a ברייתא. The ברייתא says a receipt signed by witnesses is confirmed through its signatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes no exception for where the receipt was found. It seems that once the court checks the witnesses' signatures, the receipt is valid, even if it was in the lender's possession. That goes against רב, who says such a receipt cannot be relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: A receipt or note showing a debt was paid
By its signers, through checking the signatures

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A receipt that has witnesses on it
is confirmed by means of its signers.
phrases.notes: The simple meaning is that the court checks the witnesses' handwriting, and then the receipt counts.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: סִמְפּוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו עֵדִים יִתְקַיֵּים בְּחוֹתְמָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering the oath challenge, the גמרא brings another source against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that a סמפון found with the lender cannot be relied on.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא validates a witnessed receipt just by checking signatures, with no exception for one found in the lender's possession.

steps.title: Read it as confirmed from its signers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reading the ברייתא as 'confirmed from its signers' (מחותמיו) instead of 'by its signers' (בחותמיו).
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that it reads: 'It is confirmed from its signers!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing one small letter in the ברייתא. Instead of בחותמיו it reads מחותמיו. The explanation of this reading continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'By its signers' would mean that just checking the signatures is enough. 'From its signers' means the confirmation must come from the witnesses themselves, by asking them about the receipt. So the ברייתא does not say a receipt from the lender's papers is automatically valid, and רב's view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, used to suggest reading a source differently
From its signers, meaning from the witnesses themselves

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the one-letter change: בְּחוֹתְמָיו (by its signers) versus מֵחוֹתְמָיו (from its signers). The whole answer depends on this difference.

phrases.english: Say: 'It is confirmed from its signers!'
phrases.notes: Only the first letter changes, ב becomes מ. Now the witnesses themselves must confirm it, not just their handwriting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the ברייתא in step 41.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording of the source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Checking the signatures is enough to validate the receipt, even from the lender's papers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The receipt must be confirmed by the witnesses themselves, so the ברייתא does not go against רב.
